title: Response Catalog and Synthesis Handbook
author: Priya Desai
body:
Overview

Purpose: This handbook codifies a compact, searchable catalog of incident types, decision heuristics, runbook fragments, on-call rotation constraints, game-day scenarios, and customer-facing status templates into a single operational synthesis. It is intended for first responders, bridge operators, SREs, and incident commanders at Redwood Inference.

Scope: Covers live-production inference incidents (latency spikes, KV cache failures, model-quality regressions), downstream dependency outages (datastore, auth), and cross-cutting coordination (multi-region failover, Dedicated pool exhaustion). Not a substitute for service-specific runbooks; it references and synthesizes them.

Owner and maintenance
- Document owner: Priya Desai (incident synthesis lead)
- Stewardship: Eng SRE team (quarterly review)
- Update cadence: After any P1 with > 3 hour impact or significant process change; otherwise quarterly.

How to use this handbook
1) Identify incident archetype using the "triage index" below.
2) Consult the decision ladder for immediate containment actions.
3) Apply the minimal runbook fragment to reduce customer impact.
4) Spin up the appropriate bridge cadence and populate the status template.
5) Record evidence for postmortem; use the synthesis checklist before closing.

1) Incident triage index (quick lookup)
- Latency spike: 95th percentile RPS latency > SLO by 2x for > 5 minutes across > 3% of customer tokens.
- Throughput saturation: Pod/GPU pool CPU or GPU usage > 90% and queue growth > 30% sustained for 10m.
- KV cache miss storm: Cache hit ratio drops > 40% from baseline and tail latency increases.
- Model-quality regression: Offline eval AUC or prompt set match rate drops by > 5% and customer complaints on quality observed.
- Dependency outage: Downstream error rates > 10% service-wide or auth db unavailable.
- Silent failure: No errors but traffic drops > 20% from baseline for > 10m.

2) Decision ladder (first 20 minutes)
1. Acknowledge the pager and confirm scope in the first 2 minutes. Post short status to bridge: "ACK: investigating, collecting signals (metrics/traces/logs)."
2. Identify impact tier (P1 / P2 / P3) using the triage index. If P1, escalate to incident commander (IC) within 6 minutes.
3. Run rapid health checks (script snippets below) to determine whether issue is localized.
4. If throttling or saturation suspected, apply short-term throttles or shed non-critical routes per route policy.
5. If model or KV cache suspected, route traffic to fallback compatible model variant or disable caching policy that may be causing bloom of misses.

Rapid health check examples (CLI)
- Ingress QPS and tails: curl -s "https://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=rate(requests_total[1m])" | jq .
- Pool utilization: curl -s "https://fleet.internal/api/pools/summary" | jq .
- Cache hit ratio: curl -s "https://telemetry/api/cache/hit_ratio?window=5m" | jq .

3) Containment fragments (pick minimal set)
- Throttle and shed:
  - Apply emergency rate limit to public routes exceeding error thresholds:
    1) Open Console -> Routes -> Select route -> Toggle emergency throttle -> set target qps to 60% of baseline.
    2) Inform partner teams via short bridge note.
- Model fallback:
  - Switch routing policy to a previously verified compatible variant (e.g., redwood-v1.4-quantized) for affected customers.
  - Command (pseudo-CLI): rwdctl route update --route-id R123 --model redwood-v1.4-quantized --reason "P1 fallback"
- KV cache reset (if miss storm persists):
  - For a single shard: curl -X POST "https://cache-admin.internal/shards/{shard}/invalidate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
  - If systemic, scale read replicas for KV store prior to full invalidation.

4) Bridge and comms templates
- Bridge roles (assign within 10 minutes):
  - Incident commander (IC) — overall decision maker and customer updates.
  - Bridge operator — collects and posts signals (metrics/traces/logs).
  - Engineering lead — coordinates fixes and rollbacks.
  - CS liaison — prepares customer statements and triages major accounts.

- Bridge cadence:
  - Initial post (0–10m): "Investigating increased latency across inference API. Initial scope: multiple regions, elevated 95p latency. Engineers engaged. Next update in 15 minutes."
  - Update cadence: Every 15 minutes until stabilization; then progressively to 30/60/180m as appropriate.
  - End-of-incident: Post summary, affected customers, timeline, mitigation, and next steps.

- Customer status template (short):
  - Subject: Redwood Inference — Partial service degradation affecting inference API
  - Body: "We are investigating an issue causing increased latency for inference requests in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 regions. Our engineering team has identified a service-level cause and is applying mitigations. Customers may see delays or transient errors; retry/backoff is recommended. We will provide an update by {ETA}."

- Public status page minimal payload (curl example):
curl -X POST "https://status.redwood.ai/api/v1/incidents" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"component":"inference-api","status":"degraded","impact":"partial","shortlink":"https://status.redwood.ai/incident/123","message":"Elevated latency in us-west-2; mitigations in progress"}'

5) Runbook fragments (templates for common classes)
- Latency spike (inference runtime)
  - Quick checks: check model GPU utilization, KV miss ratio, sequence-length distribution.
  - Containment: route traffic to lower-latency variant, apply route-level throttle, increase worker concurrency where safe.
  - Mitigation: patch kernel selection if regression deployed, roll back to previous model build.
  - Postmortem focus: regression cause, testing gap, rollout policy changes.

- KV cache miss storm
  - Quick checks: cache telemetry, backend datastore latency, LRU eviction rate, recent config changes.
  - Containment: pin hot prefixes, selectively invalidate problematic shards, enable read-through caching to a fallback store.
  - Mitigation: rebuild KV topology with hot-key partitioning, deploy read replicas.
  - Postmortem focus: telemetry alert thresholds, cache expiry tuning, canary for config rollout.

- Model quality regression (production-serving)
  - Quick checks: recent model rollout IDs, comparison against gold prompt set, rollback availability.
  - Containment: immediately route affected traffic to previous stable model variant; open a data-capture toggle for failing prompts.
  - Mitigation: promote rollback, isolate the training/serving difference, run a gated A/B rollout policy next.
  - Postmortem focus: evaluation coverage, rollout gate improvements, alerting on quality drift.

6) On-call rotation constraints and best practices
- Coverage model: Primary + Secondary per weekday; weekend on-call is Primary only with Secondary standing by.
- Handoff checklist (to use at shift change):
  1) Confirm bridge state (any open incidents?).
  2) Review scheduled maintenance windows and active rollouts.
  3) Validate notification routing for critical services.
  4) Share outstanding action items in the handoff channel.
- Paging thresholds: Do not escalate to on-call for single-customer low-severity chat unless error rate > 5% service-wide.
- Fatigue guardrails: No individual should be scheduled for more than 4 high-severity incidents in a 7-day window; schedule an immediate swap if the threshold is exceeded.

7) Game-day scenario cookbook (rehearsal recipes)
- Scenario: KV cache cold-start + miss storm (45m exercise)
  - Objectives: Verify shard invalidation workflow, bridge coordination, rate-limiting UI, and status page integration.
  - Inject: Simulate cache hit_ratio degradation to 30%.
  - Success criteria: Containment actions executed in < 15m; status page updated within 10m; no customer-facing SLA breach.
- Scenario: Silent-degradation (traffic drop)
  - Objectives: Validate detection of silent-failure, customer-communication pipeline, and fallback routing.
  - Inject: Drop 25% of test customers’ traffic to a region.
  - Success criteria: Detection and bridge opened in < 10m; monitoring rule refined after play.

8) Post-incident synthesis checklist (before postmortem)
- Data collection: traces, request-level logs (sampled), deployment and rollout metadata, prom-query snapshots.
- Timeline: mark acknowledges, mitigation steps, and communications.
- Evidence quality: ensure timestamps are synchronized and references to specific trace IDs are present.
- Impact accounting: list affected customers, minutes of degraded service, and SLO delta.
- Guardrail updates: if human procedure was unclear, create a short runbook fragment.

9) Postmortem template (use verbatim)
- Title: [P1] YYYY-MM-DD — Short descriptive phrase
- Summary: One-paragraph customer-facing summary describing impact and mitigation.
- Timeline: Bullet list of key events with ISO timestamps.
- Root cause: Short statement.
- Contributing factors: Bulleted list.
- Corrective actions: Owner, ETA (short/medium/long term), verification plan.
- Learnings and action items: Link to follow-ups and owners.

10) Evidence and observability requirements (table)
- Required signals: metrics (latency p50/p95/p99), error rate, queue length, GPU util, cache hit ratio, rollout ID, deployment job ID.
- Retention policy for incident evidence: 90 days as standard; extend to 365 days for customer-impacting P1s.

11) Automation patterns and recommended tooling
- Alert enrichment: attach rollout-id and commit SHA to every erroring trace.
- Rapid rollback button: Console action bound to a runbook that performs a model variant switch and notifies the bridge.
- Synthetic probes: add a scheduled prompt set that runs every 1m per region; failure of > 3 probes triggers a silent-failure alert.

Appendices
A — Quick status message snippets (choose one)
- "We are investigating increased inference latency in {region}. Engineers are applying mitigations; next update in 15 minutes."
- "Service restored in {region}. Root cause analysis underway; full postmortem to follow."

B — Example small postmortem owner assignment table
Owner | Role | ETA
Priya Desai | Incident synthesis lead | 2d for short-term action
Diego Ramos | Runtime engineer | 5d for kernel fix
Lina Chen | Observability | 7d to add synthetic probes

C — Related reference runbooks (links)
- Internal: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/kv-cache-operations
- Internal: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/model-rollbacks-and-variant-routing

D — Review history

Contact and escalation
For questions about this handbook or to request a game-day, contact incident-playbook@redwood.ai or ping #eng-sre-playbooks on Slack.
